checks.title: robots.txt is published and readable
checks.why: Robots.txt is the first file every compliant agent reads: policy plus a pointer to the sitemap.

checks.title: AI retrieval agents are allowed
checks.why: Retrieval assistants (ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot…) obey robots.txt and are the front door for agent users.

checks.title: XML sitemap is discoverable
checks.why: Sitemaps enumerate pages that are not prominently linked and tell agents what content exists.

checks.title: Sitemap lists key pages
checks.why: If pricing, docs and signup are missing from the sitemap, agents that use it find nothing.

checks.title: llms.txt is published
checks.why: A curated Markdown map (/llms.txt) is an emerging convention that lets agents ingest the site without layout parsing.

checks.title: Title and meta description in HTML
checks.why: The summary agents use to decide whether to read a page at all.

checks.title: Canonical URL is declared
checks.why: Tells agents which URL variant is authoritative across http/https, www, query-string and path variants.

checks.title: Valid JSON-LD structured data
checks.why: Unambiguous facts about the organisation and pages, readable without DOM walking.

checks.title: Navigation exposes key destinations
checks.why: Agents pick links by visible labels. If pricing, docs and signup are not linked, they are invisible on purpose-free fetches too.

checks.title: Open Graph metadata
checks.why: og:title and og:image keep link previews consistent for both humans and agents that summarise by card.

checks.title: Homepage reachable over HTTPS
checks.why: If the homepage is not reachable with a plain HTTP client, nothing else can be audited — and no agent can read the site.

checks.title: Core content is in the initial HTML
checks.why: Fetch-only agents receive the server HTML verbatim. If the content is assembled by JavaScript, they see an empty shell.

checks.title: No bot challenge on public pages
checks.why: CAPTCHAs and "verify you are human" interstials stop autonomous agents at the door even when the page would load.

checks.title: Pages are not marked noindex
checks.why: noindex is a standing instruction for retrieval systems to forget the page — often applied to catalogues or docs by accident.

checks.title: HTML is a reasonable size
checks.why: Fetchers with capped context windows truncate or drop oversized documents before the useful part is reached.

checks.title: Document language is declared
checks.why: Helps agents pick language handling for extraction, translation and locale-sensitive answers.

checks.title: Machine-readable alternate advertised
checks.why: Advertised feeds or Markdown alternatives let agents consume content without DOM parsing.

checks.title: Key pages return successful responses
checks.why: Discovered pricing, docs and signup pages must actually load with a normal agent user-agent.

checks.title: Heading structure is clear
checks.why: One h1 plus an ordered outline lets agents segment a page the way readers do.

checks.title: Semantic landmarks are used
checks.why: main, nav and footer separate content from chrome; without them agents must guess which text matters.

checks.title: Images have alt text
checks.why: Agents cannot see screenshots, diagrams or chart images — alt text is what they read.

checks.title: Links have descriptive names
checks.why: Agents choose links by their text; empty or icon-only anchors are dead ends in the link graph.

checks.title: Buttons have accessible names
checks.why: Icon-only buttons (hamburger, close, "→") cannot be reasoned about by text-only agents.

checks.title: Form fields are labelled
checks.why: Labelled fields are the only way an agent could ever (legitimately) assist with a form; placeholders alone are ambiguous.

checks.title: Navigation uses real links
checks.why: href="#" and click-handler-only "links" cannot be followed by a fetcher; only real anchors work for every agent class.

checks.title: Agent task: locate signup
checks.why: An agent helping a new customer must find the way to create an account. The task is followed with links only — never submitted.

checks.title: Agent task: locate docs or help
checks.why: Agents answer "how do I…" questions from your docs. If they cannot find them, they answer from guesses.

checks.title: Agent task: find pricing
checks.why: The most commonly delegated commercial question. If a link-following agent cannot reach pricing, it cannot answer it.

checks.title: Agent task: extract plan details
checks.why: Price, currency period and plan names as plain text — half the value of a pricing page for an agent.

checks.title: Prices present in the initial HTML
checks.why: Plan prices must exist in the server HTML; JavaScript-injected prices are missed by every fetch-only agent.

checks.title: Offers described with structured data
checks.why: schema.org Product/Offer markup states price, currency and availability without layout parsing.

checks.title: Agent task: reach the checkout interface
checks.why: Following plan CTAs to checkout is the end of the purchase journey. The auditor stops as soon as a payment interface loads and enters nothing.

checks.title: Plan CTAs are real links
checks.why: Script-only buy buttons ("Upgrade" with an onclick handler) cannot be followed by fetchers — and never appear in the link graph.
